# Implementation Plan: OCR Snipping & Summarization Application

**Branch**: `001-ocr-snipping-app` | **Date**: 2025-10-29 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)
**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/001-ocr-snipping-app/spec.md`

**Note**: This plan is generated by the `/speckit.plan` command and follows the constitution requirements defined in `.specify/memory/constitution.md`.

## Summary

Build a React 18 frontend application that enables medical associates to upload scanned PDF documents, select regions of interest using a snipping overlay, extract text via OCR, edit extracted content in organized text boxes, and generate AI-powered summaries. The application prioritizes accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA compliance), security (XSS prevention, CSRF protection), and usability (keyboard shortcuts, non-blocking UI). The technical approach uses React PDF Viewer for document rendering, Material UI for accessible components, Mock Service Worker for API stubbing during development, and comprehensive testing via Jest, Cypress/Playwright, and axe-core.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: JavaScript (ES6+) with React 18.2+
**Primary Dependencies**: React 18, React PDF Viewer (@react-pdf-viewer/core), Material UI (MUI) v5, Mock Service Worker (MSW) v2
**Storage**: N/A (session-based only, no persistence per FR-061)
**Testing**: Jest 29+ for unit tests, Cypress 13+ or Playwright 1.40+ for E2E tests, axe-core 4.8+ for accessibility testing
**Target Platform**: Modern web browsers (Chrome 90+, Firefox 88+, Safari 14+, Edge 90+) running on desktop/laptop devices
**Project Type**: Web application (frontend-only; backend APIs stubbed during development)
**Performance Goals**:
- PDF upload & initial render: <3 seconds (FR-057)
- OCR processing per region: <1.5 seconds for 90% of requests (FR-058, SC-002)
- Summarization: <3 seconds for 5 text boxes (SC-005)
- UI responsiveness: <100ms for undo/redo operations (SC-011)
- Loading indicators for operations >500ms (SC-013)

**Constraints**:
- Maximum PDF file size: 10 MB (FR-003)
- No client-side data persistence (FR-061) - security requirement for medical data
- Non-blocking UI: users can create new snips while OCR processes previous requests (FR-025, FR-059)
- WCAG 2.1 AA compliance mandatory (FR-039, FR-041)
- Keyboard-only navigation required (FR-037, SC-007)

**Scale/Scope**:
- Single-user sessions (no concurrent editing, assumption documented in spec)
- PDF documents: 1-50 pages typical, tested up to 100+ pages (edge case)
- Text boxes: 1-50 per session typical
- Session duration: 10-30 minutes per document workflow

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design.*

### Principle I: Accessibility First (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
✅ **PASS** - Functional requirements FR-032 through FR-043 mandate ARIA roles, keyboard navigation, WCAG 2.1 AA contrast (4.5:1), high-contrast mode, and screen reader support. Success criteria SC-007, SC-008, SC-012 provide measurable accessibility targets.

### Principle II: Security by Design
✅ **PASS** - Requirements FR-049 through FR-053 specify XSS prevention, CSRF tokens, HTTPS with SameSite=Strict cookies, and input sanitization. FR-061 prohibits client-side storage of medical data. FR-002, FR-003, FR-006 enforce file validation to prevent malicious uploads.

### Principle III: Modular Component Architecture
✅ **PASS** - Constitution file structure matches planned component organization: PDFUploader, PDFViewerPane, SnipOverlay, SnipList, SummarizePanel with clear separation of concerns. Each component has well-defined responsibilities per user stories.

### Principle IV: Coordinate Precision & Conversion
✅ **PASS** - Requirements FR-017, FR-018 mandate normalized coordinates (0-1 range) and y-axis inversion. Constitution explicitly calls out this as critical for usability. Will be implemented in `utils/coordinates.js` with inline math documentation per code quality standards.

### Principle V: Test-Driven Quality (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
✅ **PASS** - Testing stack defined (Jest, Cypress/Playwright, axe-core). Success criteria SC-003, SC-011, SC-012 provide testable metrics. Constitution pre-PR gates require all tests passing before merge. User story acceptance scenarios serve as test specifications.

### Principle VI: API Contract Adherence
✅ **PASS** - Constitution specifies `/api/snip-crop` and `/api/summarize` contracts. Clarification #3 updated contract to adaptive summarization (no max_sentences parameter). MSW will stub these contracts during development (FR requirement).

### Principle VII: Progressive Enhancement & Graceful Degradation
✅ **PASS** - Requirements FR-053, FR-055 mandate retry mechanisms and state preservation during failures. Clarification #4 confirms non-blocking UI with queued OCR processing. Loading indicators and aria-live announcements ensure feedback for all operations.

### Technology Stack Compliance
✅ **PASS** - All mandatory technologies from constitution Technical Standards section are included:
- React 18 ✅
- React PDF Viewer ✅
- Material UI (MUI) ✅
- React Context API for state ✅
- Mock Service Worker (MSW) ✅
- Jest, Cypress/Playwright, axe-core ✅

### Verdict
🟢 **ALL GATES PASSED** - Proceed to Phase 0 research. No constitution violations identified. No complexity justification required.

## Phase 0: Research

*Research findings to resolve implementation decisions and validate technology choices.*

### Research Tasks

1. **React PDF Viewer Plugin Architecture**
   - Research available plugins for React PDF Viewer (@react-pdf-viewer/core)
   - Evaluate toolbar, search, thumbnail, and zoom plugins
   - Document custom overlay implementation patterns

2. **Material UI Accessibility Features**
   - Research MUI accessibility best practices (focus management, ARIA)
   - Evaluate high-contrast theme customization
   - Document keyboard navigation patterns for form controls

3. **Mock Service Worker Setup**
   - Research MSW 2.x setup for React 18 applications
   - Document request handler patterns for OCR/summarization endpoints
   - Evaluate error simulation strategies for testing

4. **Coordinate Conversion Patterns**
   - Research PDF coordinate system conventions (bottom-left origin)
   - Document browser-to-PDF coordinate transformation formulas
   - Evaluate high-DPI scaling considerations

5. **Undo/Redo Implementation**
   - Research command pattern for comprehensive undo (snips + text + operations)
   - Evaluate state snapshot strategies
   - Document memory management for undo stack

6. **Non-Blocking UI Patterns**
   - Research queue management for async OCR requests
   - Evaluate loading indicator patterns (per-snip vs. global)
   - Document optimistic UI update strategies

### Research Deliverable

See [research.md](./research.md) for consolidated findings, decisions, rationales, and alternatives considered.

### API Contracts

See [contracts/](./contracts/) for OpenAPI 3.0 specifications:
- `snip-crop.yaml`: POST /api/snip-crop endpoint
- `summarize.yaml`: POST /api/summarize endpoint

**API Response Schema** (POST /api/summarize):
```json
{
  "summary": "string (generated summary text)",
  "timestamp": "ISO-8601 datetime",
  "model_version": "string (optional, for debugging)"
}
```
**Note**: Summary length is NOT returned by API; frontend derives character count client-side if needed for display.

## Post-Implementation Metrics

The following success criteria require user acceptance testing or production telemetry and are **out of scope** for initial implementation:

- **SC-003**: 85% first-attempt success rate - requires user testing with 20+ participants
- **SC-014**: 90% report reduced time - requires post-deployment survey comparing workflow times

**Recommended approach**: After MVP deployment (User Story 1), conduct user acceptance testing with 10-15 medical associates to gather baseline feedback. Deploy full feature set and run follow-up survey after 2 weeks of production usage.
